title: Escalation Playbook Refresh — Working Notes (Support/CS/SRE/Platform)
body:
Doc purpose
- This is the working scratchpad for the Escalation Playbook refresh (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) before we publish final references to Confluence.
- Capture open questions, proposed wording, coverage gaps, and cross-functional feedback (Support, CS, SRE, Platform, Docs, Legal).
- Constraint reminder: keep customer-sensitive specifics out of broad docs; ensure escalation guidance matches actual on-call rotations; SLA language must align with enterprise contracts and published coverage windows.

Owners / review
- Support Ops: Dev Patel (owner), Owen Phillips (incident/escalation SME)
- CS leadership: Jasmine Liu, Rachel Kim
- SRE: Sean Gallagher (SLO/paging alignment), Rafael Mendes (on-call + incident process)
- Platform: Priya Natarajan (sponsor), Ethan Park (control plane workflows), Mina Haddad (routing/fallback input)
- Docs/DevEx: Elliot Price (program), Wei Chen + Kira Thompson (writers)
- Legal/Compliance: Sofia Mendes (contract language), Naomi Feldman (doc sensitivity)

Target outcomes (what “done” looks like)
- One severity rubric that Support can use in Jira without re-translation by Eng.
- Tiered SLA table that is (a) achievable by Support coverage and (b) not in conflict with engineering paging thresholds or customer contract commitments.
- Clear “when to start a bridge” vs “when to move to #incidents / declare incident.”
- Escalation directory: who to page by product area, with backups + handoff rules.
- Jira field standards + automation: required fields at triage, SLA timers, consistent linking to Slack bridge + known-issues index.


SECTION A — Severity and priority language (draft)

Current pain
- Support uses P0–P4 in Jira but Engineering thinks in incident Sev (Sev0–Sev3) + SLO alerts.
- We’ve had inconsistent P1 definition: sometimes “important enterprise customer” vs “service broadly degraded.”
- Need to avoid “customer is loud => P0” while still acknowledging revenue/exec risk.

Proposal (working draft) — Support priority definitions (customer-impact oriented)
P0 (Critical / active outage)
- Criteria (one or more):
  - Hosted API: widespread inability to authenticate, generate, stream, or embed in a region OR multi-region impact.
  - Dedicated: customer’s dedicated endpoint unavailable OR sustained severe latency such that workload cannot run.
  - Private: customer environment impaired such that production traffic is down or data plane is broken post-upgrade.
  - Security/compliance incident suspected (data exposure, key compromise) => immediate security escalation (separate path).
- Expected handling:
  - Start Slack bridge immediately (or move into #incidents if already qualifies as incident).
  - Page SRE on-call when thresholds indicate platform/runtime degradation; page Platform on-call when control plane/auth/SSO/audit logs are implicated.
  - Customer update cadence is “frequent + timeboxed,” but must be contract-safe (see SLA section).

P1 (High / significant degradation or high-risk)
- Criteria examples:
  - Elevated error rates for a specific model/route/region affecting multiple customers but not full outage.
  - Enterprise customer impacted with credible risk of production downtime or contractual breach if not mitigated quickly.
  - Reproducible bug with no workaround and clear evidence it will worsen (e.g., autoscaling oscillation causing rising latency).
- Handling:
  - Bridge optional; recommended when multiple teams needed or situation evolving.
  - Page only if it crosses defined engineering alert thresholds OR if mitigation requires on-call action (capacity shift, routing config, rollback).

P2 (Medium)
- Feature impaired or intermittent issue with a workaround; limited customer scope; not trending worse.
- Default to async triage with clear next update time.

P3 (Low)
- How-to, docs, minor bug, cosmetic or low-severity confusion; no production impact.

P4 (Info/request)
- Sales/CS requests, product feedback, account housekeeping; not time-bound.

Mapping (draft) — Support P to Incident Sev
- P0 -> Sev0/Sev1 depending on blast radius
- P1 -> Sev1/Sev2
- P2 -> Sev2/Sev3
- P3/P4 -> not incident
Note: SRE asks we avoid “hard mapping” in the Support UI that implies an incident must be declared; instead provide “typical mapping” + explicit triggers for when to involve #incidents.

Open questions
- Do we need separate tagging for “Exec risk” vs “Service risk”? (Rachel prefers a field/tag; SRE concerned it biases paging.)
- Add a “customer_tier_impact” field (self_serve/dedicated/private/enterprise) to standardize urgency without overriding technical severity.

Feedback captured
- Sean: “P0 must be grounded in measurable service impact. If a single enterprise customer is down due to their proxy timeout, that’s P1/P2 unless we confirm platform-side.”
- Rafael: “If Support starts a bridge, include request IDs, region, model, last known good time, and whether customer tried retries. That determines whether to page.”
- Mina: “Routing/fallback confusion often reads as ‘pinned model ignored.’ We need a quick checklist and a dashboard link so Support doesn’t page routing immediately.”


SECTION B — SLA table (draft) and alignment concerns

Guiding principles
- Support SLA is about response and update cadence, not guaranteed fix time.
- Engineering SLOs and paging thresholds should be the trigger for incident response; Support SLAs should not force paging for non-platform issues.
- Ensure language is consistent with enterprise contracts and support coverage windows.

Working draft SLA targets (needs Sofia/Legal sign-off)
Self-serve (Hosted API)
- First response: within business hours target (not 24/7) unless status page indicates an active incident.
- Updates: “as new info available” (avoid hard commitments).
Dedicated
- First response: faster target, with on-call escalation path when dedicated endpoint is degraded.
- Updates: scheduled cadence when P0/P1.
Private
- First response: depends on support package; emphasize required diagnostics bundle to avoid delays.
Enterprise
- First response: fastest; updates on a fixed cadence during P0/P1, but language should allow “waiting on customer” pauses without “SLA stop-the-clock” confusion.

Known friction
- Slack thread debate: “every 30 min vs hourly” update cadence. CS wants 30 min for key accounts; SRE warns this becomes unsustainable during multi-incident periods and encourages shallow updates.
- Proposed compromise language: “Every 60 minutes at minimum for P0/P1 incidents during coverage hours; for executive escalations or contractual commitments, can increase to 30 minutes if incident commander/support lead agrees.”

Open questions
- “Waiting on Customer” status: do we pause SLA timers? (Support wants clarity; SRE/Legal says be careful—contracts may not allow ‘pausing’ language; we should describe it as “next update scheduled after customer provides X,” while continuing internal tracking.)
- After-hours policy: do we explicitly say “best effort” for self-serve? (Likely yes.)
- Credits requests: include a single paragraph on “Support does not commit to credits; route through exec escalation protocol.”

Notes from Sofia (Legal)
- Avoid “guarantees” in internal docs that look like external commitments.
- Use “targets” and “typical cadence” with “may vary based on incident severity and available information.”
- Ensure tier names match packaging (Dedicated vs Private vs Enterprise support add-on) — no made-up tiers.


SECTION C — Escalation paths and ownership boundaries (draft)

Goal
- Support should know who to page first based on symptom category (auth, streaming, routing, audit logs, installer upgrades, dedicated scaling).

Draft ownership (as captured from Platform thread + email)
- SRE owns:
  - Multi-customer service degradation, region instability, broad latency/error rate regressions, capacity incidents, incident command.
- Platform owns:
  - Control plane/authentication, SSO/SAML, audit logs pipeline (with SRE partnership when infra/backlog is root cause), quota/rate-limit policy + account entitlements.
- Runtime/Serving (via Platform/SRE routing depending on on-call model):
  - Streaming disconnect classifications, gateway behaviors, model runtime regressions.
- Private Deployments/Platform:
  - Installer upgrades, migrations, cluster integration issues, VPC/on-prem networking primitives (with customer env owner involvement).

Coverage gaps to resolve
- Who is the single “pagerduty escalation group” for Support when it’s unclear (INT-331)? Need a default group that can triage and redirect.
- Weekend coverage for Private installer issues: is there a formal rotation or “best effort”? (Priya N says align with existing on-call; don’t invent.)
- Dedicated autoscaling: SRE vs Platform? (Currently SRE for capacity/infra + Platform for config tooling. Need explicit split: “SRE if service instability; Platform if misconfig/feature gap.”)

Action items
- Dev to confirm final pagerduty group names and aliases with Rafael + Benji before publishing Confluence directory.


SECTION D — Slack bridge conventions + when to move to #incidents

What Support needs (from SRE)
- A pinned template for any bridge/channel:
  - Ticket: SUP-#### link
  - Customer + tier (internal name only; no sensitive details in broadly visible channels)
  - Symptom + start time + current status
  - Region + model + endpoint + SDK versions
  - Request IDs (>=3) + timestamps
  - Any recent deploy/release notes known
  - Customer mitigation tried (retries/backoff/timeouts)
  - Impact estimate (req/s, error rate, # workspaces)

Bridge naming (working)
- #sup-bridge-<short-issue>-<region>-<yyyymmdd>
- If an incident is declared: move/duplicate to #inc-<yyyymmdd>-<shortname> under incident bot process

When to escalate from bridge -> incident
- If engineering paging threshold crossed (error rate/latency SLO breach) OR multiple customers impacted OR region degradation suspected.
- Do NOT move to incident for single-customer misconfiguration unless we have evidence it’s a platform regression.

Automation requests (INT-332)
- Slack workflow to create bridge channel and auto-post the template + ask for SUP ticket link.
- Incident bot should prompt for and pin related SUP tickets (ENG-4830 / incident-bot PR).

Open question
- Who owns customer-facing updates (email) vs internal updates (Slack)? Proposal: Support owns external comms drafts; incident commander/SRE approves technical statements; CS aligns tone/exec messaging.


SECTION E — Jira field guidelines + SLA timers (draft)

Required fields at triage (proposal)
- region
- product_tier (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- endpoint type (chat/generate/embeddings/rerank/audit logs/etc)
- model + version (if applicable)
- sdk + version + language
- request_ids (min 1, target 3)
- customer impact (free text + dropdown?)
- suspected category (auth/streaming/routing/installer/audit logs/limits/other)
- links: Slack thread/bridge, dashboards, related incidents

SLA fields
- first_response_due_at
- next_update_due_at (instead of a single sla_due_at; reduces confusion on “update cadence”)

Automation ideas (INT-333)
- If priority P0/P1 and missing request_ids => comment auto-reminder + prevent “Escalated” status transition.
- If category matches known issues tags (e.g., streaming timeouts, 429 mismatch, audit log lag) => auto-suggest KB link(s) + macro snippet.
- When Support creates a bridge channel => bot posts a comment into Jira with channel link and pins ticket.

Feedback
- Dylan: keep automations simple; prefer “warn + nudge” rather than hard-blocking transitions for all teams. Suggest block only for P0/P1.


SECTION F — Draft wording snippets (to reuse in Confluence + macros)

Severity snippet (for Support to paste internally)
- “Setting priority based on observable customer impact and confirmed platform signals. If unclear whether platform-side, start at P1 and escalate to P0 only after confirming multi-request evidence + platform degradation indicators.”

Update cadence snippet (enterprise-safe)
- “We’ll provide updates at a regular cadence while we investigate and mitigate. Updates may be more frequent during active mitigation; in some cases we may schedule the next update after a specific diagnostic step is completed.”

Request ID ask (customer-safe)
- “Please share 2–3 request IDs and approximate timestamps (including timezone). If possible, include the region and model name/version. This helps us correlate your requests with platform logs.”


SECTION G — Risks / things we must not do
- Do not publish customer names, specific revenue, or internal-only incident timelines in broadly visible docs.
- Do not encourage bypassing #incidents / incident commander process.
- Do not create new SLA commitments that conflict with contracts.
- Do not instruct Support to page individual engineers directly (keep to on-call rotations and documented groups).


SECTION H — Next steps (as of last edit)
- Dev: incorporate SRE feedback on P0 definition + incident triggers; update severity draft and send for final sign-off (Sean/Rafael).
- Rachel: confirm enterprise update cadence language with Jasmine + Sofia; align with existing comms expectations.
- Priya N / Ethan: finalize ownership boundaries in escalation directory (SSO/audit logs/quota/routing).
- Dylan: implement Jira “required fields” + SLA reminders (scope: P0/P1 first).
- Elliot + writers: rewrite playbook sections into Confluence-ready pages; ensure consistent terminology across pages.
- All: validate the bridge template in one real escalation (target: streaming disconnects + 429 mismatch tickets).

Change log
- 2026-02-02: Initial scratchpad created (Dev)
- 2026-02-05: Added draft P0/P1 definitions + SRE notes (Dev)
- 2026-02-07: Added SLA cadence debate + Legal cautions (Rachel/Dev)
- 2026-02-10: Added Jira automation ideas and required fields (Dylan/Dev)
- 2026-02-14: Added updated ownership boundaries + risks section (Priya N/Dev)
